purpose: Conservative selected Vulkan backend device and queue initialization; not a native D3D12 device
admission: All existing hard and conditional startup inventory requirements must be satisfied
Conventional million-per-stage sampled-image/storage-image/storage-buffer limits; no unobserved descriptor-buffer alternative
robustBufferAccess, timelineSemaphore, bufferDeviceAddress, synchronization2 and dynamicRendering must each be supported
First nonempty family supporting both graphics and compute; Vulkan graphics/compute queues implicitly support transfer operations
Exact existing selected Lightning LUID/node/matching physical device and sibling loader/ICD contract

optional_presentation_extensions.condition: Exact selected ICD advertises Win32 surfaces and selected device advertises swapchains

enable_chain: VkDeviceCreateInfo.pNext -> VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 -> Vulkan11 -> Vulkan12 -> Vulkan13 -> Robustness2; pEnabledFeatures NULL; every unlisted feature zero

operations: empty vkQueueSubmit2 with monotonic private timeline signal

teardown: Rust serializes queue/creation/retirement. QueueWaitIdle after any submission attempt; ordinary failed drain retains owner/device/backend for retry; VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST permits object teardown. Destroy semaphore before device, then instance, ICD/loader, runtime callback context.
limitations: Not the complete vkd3d device feature set or bindless implementation
No shader translation, descriptors, resource/memory/residency bridge, command-list translation, rendering or presentation
No native DDI device/table, advertised version, feature level or application-facing d3d12.dll replacement
The private timeline remains distinct from a D3D12 fence. A separate experimental owned-mapping native fence bundle connects actual observed completion to KMT signals and asynchronous OS wait events
Modeled dependency tests do not establish real Venus, native Windows runtime or GPU execution acceptance
